claims.head: A tough night ahead for Laferriere
claims.call: The Islanders’ P2 (Pelech and Pulock) spends at least 49% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Islanders keep sending Pelech and Pulock out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter DeBoer has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Kings’ second line is Perry, Haula and Laferriere.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 3 of their last 5 games, including the last one. Corey Perry takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Joel Edmundson is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Doughty and Ceci.
Kevin Fiala is on injured reserve (lower-leg surgery) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Alex Turcotte is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Mats Zuccarello is out and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Jared Wright was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Joel Armia and Scott Laughton.
Quinton Byfield is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 43% last season.

Mathew Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Victor Eklund has taken his spot beside Brayden Schenn and Calum Ritchie.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 37% last season.

NYI.head: A genuine toss-up
NYI.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, the Islanders have home-ice advantage, and Los Angeles will be without Fiala. The Islanders can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

LAK.head: Nothing to separate these two
LAK.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, the Islanders have home-ice advantage, and Los Angeles will be without Fiala. For the Kings, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.
